introduction.heading: Plumbing for Kaysville homes
introduction.body:
Half of the homes in Kaysville were built in 1994 or later, and about 30% before 1980, according to the U.S. Census Bureau. Many of those homes are reaching the age when water heaters, faucets and fixtures need replacing. A water heater usually lasts 10 to 15 years.

Kaysville buys all of its drinking water from the Weber Basin Water Conservancy District: Weber River and creek water treated at the district's plants, supplemented by groundwater, mainly from the Delta Aquifer. Hardness ranges from 10 to 18 grains per gallon (171 to 308 mg/L), according to the Weber Basin Water Conservancy District's 2025 water quality report. The U.S. Geological Survey classes that as hard to very hard water. Hard water leaves mineral deposits in water heaters, faucets and appliances, and a water softener or filtration system cuts that buildup.

About 94% of Kaysville properties also have a separate secondary irrigation supply, from three independent irrigation companies.
